methodological_rigor.justification: A planning study comparing four radiotherapy techniques (CO-IMRT, NONCO-IMRT, CO-VMAT, NONCO-VMAT) in 48 post-thymoma patients with each patient serving as their own control across all four plans, a reasonable design for dosimetric comparison. CTV/PTV margins, OAR definitions, and plan constraints are explicit, and Monte Carlo dose calculation is used. Limitations include single-center cohort, lack of plan anonymization or independent review, and no validation with measured clinical outcomes. The NTCP analysis uses Lyman-Kutcher-Burman parameters borrowed from other tumor types, which the authors acknowledge.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: A purely dosimetric/modeling study with no patient-outcome endpoints maps to Oxford LoE 5 (mechanistic/modeling reasoning). Findings (NONCO-VMAT preferred for multi-organ protection, CO-VMAT avoids unnecessary breast irradiation) provide plausible planning guidance but do not demonstrate clinical benefit; translation requires outcome studies with pneumonitis, cardiac events, and secondary malignancy endpoints.

reporting_quality.justification: No recognized checklist clearly applies to a dosimetric planning study (CONSORT/STROBE/TRIPOD etc. are ill-fitting); the authors provide adequate method detail for beam geometry, constraints, LKB model, and statistical testing, but omit key elements: start/end date range (redacted), patient selection flow, how plans were optimized (same planner? single attempt?), and raw dosimetric data. No data or code availability, no supplementary DVH data, and the patient enrolment dates are redacted in methods.

novelty_literature.justification: Incremental extension of prior non-coplanar work to the thymoma setting specifically comparing NONCO-VMAT against NONCO-IMRT and coplanar variants; He et al. 2022 already reported CO-VMAT breast dose issues. The demonstration that NONCO-VMAT can recover IMRT-comparable breast sparing while preserving VMAT heart/spinal cord advantages adds a meaningful but narrow contribution to the planning literature.

writing_presentation.justification: Manuscript is competent and structured clearly; tables and figures appear informative. The EUD formula is referenced ('where vi is the relative volume...') without the equation actually being rendered, a notable technical omission. Units are inconsistent (dose values reported without explicit Gy in Results text), and the methods section misses a date range due to redaction but the text would have read awkwardly regardless. Overall readable but technical completeness is modest.

key_strengths: Systematic within-patient comparison of four planning techniques across 48 thymoma patients with identical PTV coverage criteria
Inclusion of LKB-based NTCP analysis in addition to DVH metrics provides biological contextualization
Clear practical message: NONCO-VMAT combines VMAT advantages (lower heart V30, spinal cord/esophagus Dmax) with IMRT-like breast sparing
Technical detail on beam/couch configurations is sufficient for replication
key_concerns: Planning-study design provides no clinical outcome validation; the two patients with pneumonitis are anecdotal and not incorporated in any outcome analysis
NTCP parameters borrowed from other tumor settings (breast, NSCLC, lymphoma) without sensitivity analysis on parameter choice
EUD equation referenced in text but not rendered in the manuscript; several values reported without units in Results
No data/code availability, no patient enrolment date range, and no checklist reporting
Modest novelty; similar findings on CO-VMAT breast dose previously reported by He et al. 2022
chief_reviewer.rationale: A competent but incremental dosimetric/NTCP planning study with modest novelty and no clinical outcome validation; appropriate for a lower-tier specialty medical-physics or radiotherapy journal after minor revisions to render the EUD formula and clarify units and data availability.
